correctness.rationale: The block-cut tree of a cactus allows rooted terminal-block contractions; explicit four-cycle folding is graph-1-Lipschitz and moves vertices at most one, and whole pentagons collapse with move at most two. Kuribayashi Theorem 3.9 turns these into d_IHC upper bounds. H_0 at scales below one gives lower bound one-half. The cycle retraction together with a signed nearest-displacement integral cocycle on N(C_n)(2) gives nonzero H_1(1)->H_1(2) and lower bound one for each n>=5. All claimed boundary inclusions and scopes are checked; 23 deterministic finite verifications corroborate but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The uniform exact d_IHC phase transition depends only on whether a cactus has a pentagonal block (when longer blocks are excluded) rather than on its diameter, number of blocks or branches. This separates a structural topological obstruction from a coarse radius bound using a natural two-parameter class. The explicit relative 4-cycle contraction and signed persistent winding obstruction explain why the 5-cycle threshold is sharp, providing a meaningful limit case for applying enriched-nerve interleaving theory.
